messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — after the AWQ roll I reproduced a P95 regression on GPUs for long-context chat (>2048). GPU mem shows short-lived churn bursts.
ajay: Can you paste the profiler snippet? GPU-bound or CPU?
maria: GPU. Trimmed flame:
```
Kernel | calls | avg ms | mem delta
matmul_opt | 110 | 1.9 | +10 MB
kv_lookup | 260 | 0.42 | +44 MB
alloc_slab | 22 | 0.6 | +72 MB
kv_evict | 6 | 2.9 | -60 MB
```
kevin: That alloc_slab +72MB spikes — smells like allocator fragmentation. Our compact slab path isn't reclaiming contiguous chunks fast enough under AWQ per-layer qparams.
sophia: Did we change the KV cache dtype anywhere? I remember a run where switching KV to fp32 reduced upcasts with AWQ->FP8 transitions.
maria: Current canary uses fp16 KV. I tried fp32 on one shard: GPU high-water rose ~400MB but p95 fell ~12ms.
ajay: So it's a trade: allocate more KV up-front to avoid per-token upcasts/rehashing overhead. Any kernel selector fallback logs?
maria: Yes — when sequences cross ~3k tokens and concurrency hits 3, selector flips from matmul_opt -> matmul_generic. Perf-bot raised a regression: :warning: perf-regression 1799854321 matmul_generic fallback.
perf-bot: [auto] Regression detected: P95 +20% for model/gptq-awq-13b on g5.xlarge. trace=tr-1799854321
kevin: Selector hysteresis + allocator fragmentation -> thrash. We should either bias selector toward low-mem kernels when fragmentation high, or increase per-stream workspace cap to let matmul_opt survive.
sophia: What's the current workspace_cap?
maria: 64MB/stream. Quick test: bumping to 128MB/stream returned p95 almost to baseline, but RSS rose. Throughput flat.
ajay: Bumping workspace masks fragmentation; we should also fix allocator reclaim: enable compact_coalesce and lower deferred_free_window to allow faster coalescing, plus reuse_buffers on attention temps.
kevin: Agree. reuse_buffers gave ~7% token latency win in prior benches. Also tune background compaction sweep interval to 500ms.
maria: Ran a 2h canary across 4 nodes (bursty QPS, random seqs). Metrics captured: p50/p95, tps, GPU high-water, fragmentation=(free_chunks/total_chunks), reclaim_latency.
Results:
- Config A (canary baseline): p95=148ms, tps=4720, GPU high=24.6GB, fragmentation=0.44, reclaim_latency=38ms
- Config B (fp32_kv + workspace=128 + reuse_buffers=true): p95=130ms, tps=4765, GPU high=25.4GB, fragmentation=0.23, reclaim_latency=21ms
- Config C (fp16_kv + workspace=64 + compact_coalesce=true): p95=135ms, tps=4740, GPU high=24.9GB, fragmentation=0.14, reclaim_latency=19ms
ajay: Config C has lowest fragmentation but matmul_generic still triggered occasionally. Config B reduces kernel switch frequency but costs ~800MB GPU.
kevin: Let's try combined B+C (fp32_kv + workspace=128 + compact_coalesce + reuse_buffers) in a short prod canary; might give additive benefit.
sophia: Also propose a per-model KV dtype policy at load-time: decide fp16 vs fp32 based on model quant type (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) and historical token mix. Avoid global knob.
ajay: We can infer break-even from previous evals — add to model onboarding.
maria: Found a bug: deferred_free_window didn't wake compactor if worker queue was full. Filed PR #4610 to fix. Also PRs: #4611 (reuse_buffers), #4612 (selector debug logs).
perf-bot: [auto] Created issue perf/1799854321: investigate kernel selector hysteresis. Assigned: kevin, priority: high.
kevin: I'll run a parameter sweep across (workspace_cap, reuse_buffers, selector_memory_bias) and post results tomorrow.
sophia: If B+C proves good, define defaults: default for standard customers = fp16_kv + compact_coalesce, premium = fp32_kv + larger workspace. And add auto-tuner for model-level KV dtype.
ajay: Next action: run combined config in 24h canary and collect detailed allocator traces + kernel selector inputs (mem_free, recent_latency, concurrency). Add small profiler hook to log selector decision inputs.
maria: On it — will attach perf graphs and the selector input traces here. Summary: root cause = allocator fragmentation + aggressive memory checks in kernel selector; mitigations = buffer reuse, compact coalescing, larger workspace for select tiers, and model-based KV dtype policy.
kevin: Thanks all. Please report back in this thread after the 24h canary. :thumbsup:
